Each goal can be entered by its full name or a short keyword for fast

commitResults.messageTitle: List and rank compatible clients with find match/INDEX
commitResults.messageBody:
find match/INDEX lists every client compatible with the client at
INDEX, best matches first. It reuses MatchAssessment from the match
command, so the two commands never disagree: pairs assessed as
incompatible are hidden, clients with unknown details stay listed, and
the rest are ranked by preferences met in both directions.

ModelManager now exposes a SortedList over its FilteredList so the
displayed order can be ranked; list and other searches reset it.
Add named client groups and matching shortlists

The main window was still titled "Address App" and used the AB3

commitResults.messageTitle: Lay out main window and match result as mockups
commitResults.messageBody:
The mockups label the command box and client list, show compact result
feedback, and present a match as an overall verdict followed by
requirement tables.

Add "Command" and "Client list" captions and pad the window content.
Wrap long feedback text and start the result box at two rows, so short
messages no longer leave empty space.

Show a match as an "Overall result" box with the outcome and a one-line
reason, then a three-column table per direction: requirement, the other
client's value, and assessment. Hide the client list while a match is
shown so the tables have room at 1280x720. Any other command, including
a failed one, shows the list again.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split client cards into labelled columns
commitResults.messageBody:
Cards listed every field on its own line, so they were hard to scan.
They also used AB3's 150px column width to size the cell, which left
a large empty band below each card at normal window widths.

Arrange each card as a header with the index and name, then Details,
Attributes and Partner criteria columns. Show tags and groups as chips
in a strip below the columns. Show unrecorded attributes as "not set"
and empty criteria lists as "none". Keep every field, including the
client's own relationship goal, labelled "Goal".

Bind each card's width to the list's width, so wrapped text reports
its real height and long names, addresses and tags wrap without a
horizontal scrollbar.

commitResults.messageTitle: Switch to a light theme with a rose accent
commitResults.messageBody:
The mockups use a light layout: white panels, thin grey borders and
dark text. The dark AB3 theme no longer matched them or the product.

Replace DarkTheme.css with LightTheme.css. It uses one small palette:
primary and muted text, a grey border, a light panel colour and a rose
accent for focus, selection, tags and failed match requirements.
Restyle the menus, scroll bars, dialogs and help window to match. Use
a red border on the command box to show a failed command.

Attributes and Partner criteria columns. Note that unrecorded values
show "not set" on the card but "Not specified" in command feedback.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use system font at three sizes for readability
commitResults.messageBody:
Text was small and used up to eight font sizes, from 10px to 17px.
Captions were hard to read, especially at 100% scaling, and the mix of
sizes made the hierarchy noisy.

Use the platform's standard UI font ("System") and limit text to three
sizes: 13px for captions, chips and table headers, 15px for body text,
and 18px for client names, the match outcome and dialog headings. Set
the body size once on the root so the other rules inherit it. Update
Ui.png to show the new type.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Arial to stop letters overlapping and clipping
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX renders the macOS system font with tight spacing, so letter
pairs ran together ("rn" read as "m") and italic text showed upright.
At the 450px minimum width, attribute labels also broke mid-word and
the "PARTNER CRITERIA" caption was cut off.

Use Arial, which ships with Windows and macOS and renders with even
spacing. Stop attribute labels from wrapping, and raise the window's
minimum width to 640px so all three card columns fit. That is still
well below the 853px logical width of 1280x720 at 150% scaling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Confine application data to the JAR home folder
commitResults.messageBody:
Working-directory paths and JavaFX caches can escape the folder
containing the JAR, violating Constraint-Data-Sandbox and risking
unrelated files. Resolve packaged data, preferences, rotating logs,
and runtime caches under the JAR home instead.

Reject traversal and outward symbolic links before file access.
Keep runtime settings process-local rather than changing the OS;
retain fixture-path support for class-directory development runs.
Document storage boundaries and manual checks in both guides, and
reconcile religion examples with the merged required-age feature.

goal features. Java 25 checks and packaged regression probes pass.

partner criteria from commands, records and cards.

Reject obsolete prefixes rather than treating them as field text.

update the user and developer guides with the transition behavior.

Refs #51

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject linked runtime caches and clarify guidance
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX accesses cache files without the application data-path checks. A
non-link-following startup walk can miss outward children hidden by an
inward directory link.

Reject every symbolic link in the private runtime folders before
configuring JavaFX. Keep normal in-home data links supported, and never
delete existing contents on rejection. A stricter cache-only policy
avoids following linked trees and handling directory cycles.

Add regressions for ordinary caches and linked root/descendant layouts.
Correct legacy religion-prefix help, duplicate command parameters and
UG/DG descriptions to match the integrated criteria behavior.

Java 25 checks pass with 404 tests. Packaged launches reject all four
linked-cache fixtures while ordinary packaged regression checks pass.

Fixes #84.

Several religion tests expose mutable temporary-folder fields and use
ambiguous collection names or array continuation formatting. A test
Javadoc also describes the wrong method after earlier integration.

Use package-private fixtures and plural collection names. Store invalid
inputs in immutable lists to avoid conflicting array indentation rules.
Move the comment to the string test and explain criteria merging in the
edit descriptor without changing application behavior.

Leave guide corrections to PR #83 and the runtime-cache fix to PR #85,
avoiding duplicate changes and published-history rewrites.

Religion data is described in prose, but existing model diagrams omit
the distinction between a client's own religion and partner criteria.

Add a focused class diagram showing optional own religion, the separate
criteria maps, and the shared normalization dependency. Keep unrelated
members out so the diagram remains readable, and show criteria as
strings rather than implying extra Religion object associations.

Commit the PlantUML source and rendered image, and embed the figure with
alternative text and an explanation in the Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore command state when saving fails
commitResults.messageBody:
A rejected deletion retained its in-memory change, so retrying the unchanged displayed index could delete a second client. Capture client/group data and view state before execution and restore them on save errors, preserving live observable-list bindings and safe retry indexes.

Cover save-failure recovery with focused regressions and document both recovery and the JavaFX launch-path restriction without changing feature or storage-loading policies.
